authority.legal_name: Auckland Transport (AT), the region's public transport authority, contracting Fullers360 as the Waitematā Harbour & Hauraki Gulf ferry operator under a public-private partnership
authority.geography_type: a sheltered harbour (the Waitematā) opening into an island-studded gulf (the Hauraki Gulf)
authority.home_waters_label: the Waitematā Harbour and the Hauraki Gulf

mandate.summary: Auckland Transport plans and funds the region's public transport, including the ferry network operated by Fullers360 across the Waitematā Harbour and Hauraki Gulf. The joint priority is decarbonizing the ferry fleet while growing capacity on busy commuter runs and connecting the Gulf islands.
current_priorities: Decarbonizing the ferry fleet under Auckland's climate plan — electric and hybrid vessels are already entering service
Growing capacity on the busy Devonport and Waiheke commuter runs
Faster, cleaner connections to the wider Hauraki Gulf without new road infrastructure

policy_targets.interim_target: Auckland's regional climate plan (Te Tāruke-ā-Tāwhiri) targets roughly halving emissions by 2030 on the path to net zero by 2050; New Zealand's Zero Carbon Act sets net zero by 2050 nationally
policy_targets.vision: Te Tāruke-ā-Tāwhiri (Auckland's Climate Plan) and the NZ Zero Carbon Act — a low-carbon transport system in which the ferry network is a decarbonization priority, not an afterthought
policy_targets.relevance: A zero-emission foiling tier advances Auckland's 2030 and 2050 climate targets directly while adding faster, higher-frequency commuter and island connections the diesel fleet cannot match.

precedent.headline: Auckland has already put zero-emission ferries on the water.

existing_program.program: Electric/hybrid ferry rollout under an AT–Fullers360 public-private partnership
existing_program.vessels: Auckland's first plug-in electric-hybrid fast ferries have entered service on inner-harbour commuter routes (Devonport and beyond), with more arriving 2025–2026
existing_program.proof_stat: New electric-hybrid vessels are projected to remove roughly 1,900 tonnes of CO2 per year on short inner-harbour runs
existing_program.note: Establishes AT and Fullers360 as committed to zero-emission ferries — the foiling tier extends that to faster, longer Gulf legs.

interpretation_for_navier: Auckland is not being asked to believe in electric ferries — it already runs them, under a formal AT–Fullers360 partnership with a regional climate mandate. What is missing is a tier that is clean AND faster: a foiling hull that speeds the busy Devonport and Waiheke commutes and opens the longer Gulf legs (Gulf Harbour, Great Barrier) that are slow and costly on diesel. Lead with the live commuter core, then reach across the Gulf.

domestic_pairs.rationale: The busiest commuter run across the Waitematā; foiling adds speed and frequency on the network's core leg, zero-emission.
The flagship Waiheke commute — Auckland's highest-demand ferry corridor; a faster clean crossing serves a fast-growing island population.
Eastern-suburbs commuter link across the harbour; foiling cuts the crossing and relieves road congestion.
Upper-harbour commuter corridor to a fast-growing residential area; clean fast passenger service without new roads.
Short North Shore commuter connector; ideal for quiet, frequent electric foiling.
Longer Whangaparāoa commuter run that is slow and costly on diesel — exactly the leg foiling efficiency unlocks.
Access to the Rangitoto/Motutapu island reserves; quiet foiling suits a sensitive conservation destination.
The long outer-Gulf run to Great Barrier (Aotea) — a Quanta-LR line-haul that makes a slow, weather-exposed connection viable and clean.

regional_links.note: The case stands on the Auckland commuter and Gulf network; there is no cross-border regional link.

routing_hazards.instruction: Every leg must be routed through navigable harbour and gulf water only — no crossing the North Shore, Waiheke or the mainland isthmus. Provide explicit hand waypoints around headlands and the harbour bridge.

hazards.detail: Upper-harbour legs (Hobsonville, ful-d04) must transit under/around the harbour-bridge span and follow the charted channel; the inner harbour is busy with recreational and commercial traffic.
Gulf-bound legs (Waiheke, Gulf Harbour, Rangitoto) must route via the Rangitoto Channel clear of North Head and reefs; never straight-line across islands.
The Gulf is a protected marine park with seabird and marine-mammal habitat; low-wake foiling is an advantage but route to charted channels and observe any protected zones.
The Great Barrier (Aotea) run (ful-d08) crosses open, weather-exposed outer-gulf water; schedule and route with weather-aware waypoints.
Half Moon Bay, Hobsonville and Matiatia have tidal approaches; route to charted wharf channels.
